target_claim_or_section: Break-even assets MD-5 $1.46B base at 20 bps; MD-5 beats MD-1 ($2.11B)
challenge: breakEvenAssets = (F + n*S)/(r - v/B) leaves out capital recovery and acquisition costs. Build ($1.94M) is carried in ModeEconomics.Build but never amortised. OnetimePerSponsor/OnetimePerAcct (onboarding and migration, $36k per sponsor plus $2.67 per account) are computed but never used. CAC and the cost of capital are also missing. So "break-even" is operating contribution only, and it favours modes that own the platform over MD-1 (build 0).
evidence: Rerun via fsx on the model DLL. MD-5 at 20 bps: $1.465B base; +build amortised over 5 yrs ($388k/yr) -> $1.70B; +CAC $125k x 5 sponsors over 5 yrs and onboarding -> $1.80B; +$300k/yr SOC 1/2 audit and insurance -> $1.98B; +10% capital charge on $8.8M -> $2.51B. Build alone cuts the MD-5 vs MD-1 advantage from $0.65B to $0.41B.
proposed_change: Report fully loaded break-even beside operating break-even: amortise build, onboarding/migration and CAC over a stated life and add a capital charge. Restate CLM-013 as "$1.7-2.0B fully loaded" and the MD-1 gap accordingly.

target_claim_or_section: Capital = deepest cumulative deficit over 60 months; lowest self-sustaining capital ~$4-5M (ER-7 P50 $5.06M)
challenge: The cash model has no customer churn and no implementation/go-live lag: licence revenue starts at full run-rate on signing. It also has no ramp of migrated accounts or AUM, assumes cash on invoice with no billing in arrears or bad debt, and holds no operating reserve. A trough with zero buffer is the minimum ever-observed balance, not the amount to raise.
evidence: Python replica reproduces ER-4/5/7 base ($6.17M/$8.82M/$4.84M). Adding 10%/yr churn, a 6-month go-live lag (9 for ER-5), 3-month arrears and a 12-month account ramp gives ER-4 $8.52M, ER-5 $12.16M and ER-7 $6.86M, and none turns cash-positive within 60 months. MC share never cash-positive: ER-7 12%->60%, ER-4 17%->75%, ER-5 38%->96%. A 6-month burn reserve adds a further $0.66M (ER-7) to $1.14M (ER-5).
proposed_change: Add churn, go-live lag, account/AUM ramp, billing terms and a bad-debt line to Routes.fs. Report capital as trough plus 6-9 months reserve. Restate the self-sustaining figure as ~$6.5-8M (ER-7) until a channel partner and implementation timelines are evidenced.

target_claim_or_section: Monte Carlo P10/P50/P90 with independent parameters
challenge: Adverse drivers are economically correlated. Slow sales go with lower price and later revenue. Higher touch rates go with longer minutes, higher activity and higher fixed staffing. Independent draws cancel these out and compress P90 and the never-covers share. The docs say correlation "would widen the tails" but never quantify it.
evidence: Gaussian-copula rerun (adverse-direction loading on a common factor). MD-5 20 bps P90 $2.20B -> $2.82B (rho 0.3) -> $3.67B (rho 0.6). MD-5 10 bps never-covers-variable-cost 3% -> 10% -> 15%, and P90 becomes "never". Routes at rho 0.5: ER-7 P90 $6.70M -> $7.92M, never-positive 12% -> 20%; ER-4 P90 $8.57M -> $9.91M, never 17% -> 25%. P50s barely move, so the headline P50 hides the tail.
proposed_change: Run the MC with a stated correlation structure (at least rho 0.3-0.5 on a demand factor and an operating-difficulty factor) and present P90 under correlation as the capital-planning figure.

target_claim_or_section: MD-5 vendor fixed $2.3M (PR87 lower bound + $0.1M AI governance)
challenge: The MD-6 basis itemises SOC 2/pen-test, insurance, sales and support, but the MD-5 basis itemises nothing. For a full outsourced administrator, sponsors' auditors need a SOC 1 Type II as well as SOC 2. A full administrator also needs crime/fidelity, E&O and cyber cover, segregation-of-duties staffing and a sales function. These are not visible, and running a full administrator costs only $0.7M more than licensing (MD-6). Fixed cost is flat from 1 to 10 sponsors and from $0.9B to $10B+ AUM, with no step costs. In ER-5 custodial=Y is parsed (Inputs.fs) but never used: there is no custody/trust partner fee, bond or regulatory capital.
evidence: Inputs.fs parses Custodial; no other module references it. MD-5 basis text compared with MD-6 basis text. Putting $300k/yr of audits and insurance outside the $2.3M moves 20 bps break-even $1.46B -> $1.65B. The MC 10 bps P90 ($10.9B, ~44k accounts) is served by the same $2.3M fixed.
proposed_change: Publish a line-item fixed-cost build for MD-5 (roles x loaded pay, SOC 1+2, insurance, sales, custody partner). Add step-fixed costs per sponsor and per AUM band. Either model the custodial flag or drop it.

target_claim_or_section: "Balance dominates"; tornado ranks avg_balance first; base $1.46B headline
challenge: The tornado leaves out fixed cost, which is the largest single driver. On its own range ($1.9-3.5M) MD-5 20 bps break-even swings $1.22B-$2.19B ($0.96B), more than balance ($0.78B). The base case also sits below the model's own P10 ($1.46B vs MC P10 $1.48B), because most ranges are skewed adverse (fixed 1.9/2.3/3.5; touch 0.6/1/2; activity 0.6/1/2.06). The same holds for registry RA-1 (base $115k vs P50 $127k) and ER-4 (base $6.17M vs P50 $6.53M).
proposed_change: Add fixed cost to the tornado and rewrite "balance dominates" as "fixed cost and balance dominate". Lead every headline with the MC P50 (and P90), and label the base case as about P5-P10 of the distribution.

target_claim_or_section: Technology-only licensing (MD-6) breaks even at ~30k accounts at $81/account; cheapest mode for the vendor
challenge: Break-even is vendor-side only. $81 is Ren's price anchor, not a willingness-to-pay derivation. The sponsor carries 97% of event minutes, all onboarding and migration, and the change risk. The sponsor saving exists only if sponsor staff hit AI-native touch rates the vendor does not control and the sponsor removes ~14.5 FTE per 10k accounts (183 -> 26 min/acct). A 3% vendor share of event minutes for a white-label vendor (L2 support, releases, sponsor configuration) is thin, and vendors normally carry implementation.
evidence: fsx: sponsor-borne cost under MD-6 = $81 + $58 event + $20 reserved/rails vs $344 MD-1 system variable. A sponsor already paying Ren ~$81 gets $0 licence saving, so the case rests entirely on headcount reduction. Vendor share at 15% plus vendor-borne implementation ($36k + $2.67/acct = ~$63k per 10k-account sponsor, 1/yr) moves break-even 29.6k -> ~35.8k accounts (+21%).
proposed_change: Build a sponsor P&L/payback (switching cost, parallel run, contract exit, realised vs paper FTE savings, ramp to native touch rates) and derive price from it. Set the vendor support/implementation share from comparable licensing vendors, not 3%.

target_claim_or_section: Lowest defensible registry run cost ~$90-120k/yr for one sponsor (RA-1 $115k)
challenge: RA-1 zeroes RC-10, including the insurance rider, even though the registry's facts drive grant-eligibility decisions with 4966 exposure. It cuts counsel to 30 h a year and carries no on-call engineering, security, pen-test or SOC share, so it is a marginal cost resting on a platform whose fixed cost absorbs those items unstated. The 0.25 FTE "named owner" priced at $67.69/h is a fraction of a compliance officer who must exist elsewhere.
evidence: fsx Registry.cost: RA-1 $115.4k. Adding a $10k rider, 60 h counsel and 0.1 FTE on-call engineering plus $15k SOC/pen-test share gives $175.1k (+52%), and $207.6k at an 8% change rate.
proposed_change: State that RA-1 is marginal cost conditional on shared platform controls and name which fixed-cost line carries them. Give a standalone-equivalent figure (~$170-210k). Keep RC-10 conditional rather than zero until OQ-009 (TPSP) is resolved.

target_claim_or_section: Charity vetting MD-5 cost $4.82/acct; registry run cost vs administration fixed cost
challenge: The event model charges vetting only $0.16 external per check (9 x 0.16 = $1.44/acct-yr). The registry run cost from doc 05 ($115k/yr for one sponsor, $1.65/grant) does not appear in events.csv, and the MD-5 fixed-cost basis does not say whether it is included. Either the registry is unfunded in the administration economics, or its omission was not stated.
evidence: At break-even (~5,860 accounts, ~53k grants) the $0.16/check external line gives ~$8.4k/yr vs RA-1 $115k. Adding $115k to MD-5 fixed moves 20 bps break-even $1.465B -> $1.534B (+$0.07B). Registry establishment ($306k) is likewise not visibly in build.
proposed_change: Add an explicit registry line (run and establishment) to MD-5/6/7 fixed or to event external cost, or cite where it sits in the $2.3M.

target_claim_or_section: Shared registry ~$14-27k per sponsor at 10 sponsors
challenge: Per-sponsor cost depends on union_exponent=0.5 (10 sponsors x 20k charities -> 63k distinct charities), an untested ASSUMPTION. Mid-size sponsors with different donor bases may overlap far less.
evidence: fsx: RA-4 at 10 sponsors, union exponent 0.5 -> $27.4k per sponsor; at 0.8 (still within the stated range) -> $45.1k (+65%).
proposed_change: Run the Schedule I overlap test (ren_schedule_i_recipient_overlap.py) before quoting per-sponsor sharing economics, and quote the range at exponent 0.3-0.8.

target_claim_or_section: Prevention saves $33.5/acct on top of native touch rates; "no double counting"
challenge: Native touch rates are calibrated to replays of designed systems, and prevention is then applied again. EV-E10 p_native 0.09 comes from the measured 7.4-11.2% routed-to-person proxy; 40% prevention cuts it to 5.4%, below the measured range. EV-E08 p_native 0.0117 x 0.5 prevention = 0.0059, which is the "~5 reviews per 1000 grants change-driven" estimate. The native rate looks back-solved, so the "prevention value" of vetting is circular.
evidence: results.md §6: E10 prevention value $10.48/acct; removing it raises MD-5 variable cost by 0.42 bps and break-even by ~2.6% (~$0.04B). Effect is small, but the decomposition claim (prevention $33.5 vs AI $17.5) is not separable as presented.
proposed_change: State whether proxy touch rates already embed the prevention mechanisms. If they do, set prev_efficacy to 0 for E08/E10 and re-attribute the saving in the decomposition.

target_claim_or_section: Labour = minutes x loaded rate (FTE cost/1800 h)
challenge: Labour is costed as perfectly divisible minutes at 100% productive utilisation of 1800 h. At break-even (~5,860 accounts x 26 min = ~2,540 h = 1.4 FTE), queue coverage, PTO and segregation of duties (three-person release, independent reconciler) force whole people. Realistic touch utilisation is 60-70%.
evidence: fsx: dividing MD-5 event labour ($28.74/acct) by 0.65 utilisation moves 20 bps break-even $1.465B -> $1.522B. A minimum ops/compliance staffing floor would add more unless it is already in fixed cost, which the MD-5 basis does not show.
proposed_change: Apply a utilisation factor (0.65-0.75) to variable labour and state a minimum staffing floor per mode in fixed cost.
